title: Density clustering links unusual radiotherapy QA signals to maintenance records
summary: DBSCAN identified unusual changes in longitudinal imaging-detector QA measurements from nine radiotherapy accelerators. Several flagged output, beam-profile and apparent jaw-position changes coincided with documented maintenance or calibration. These are retrospective measurement associations, not proof that maintenance caused a physical fault or that the system detects clinically dangerous failures.
organization: Automated Quality Assurance Consortium; Cedars-Sinai; Calvary Mater Newcastle; Emory University; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; University of Michigan

source_review.scope: Read actual primary acquisition/service-data scope, DBSCAN operation and parameter rule, source-specific outlier/service Results, independent-comparison limits and Discussion. Original canonical primary publication date October 29 is distinguished from November collection/index date. No operational treatment instructions represented. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 2018–2024 EPID QA measurements and service histories from nine TrueBeam accelerators across six institutions. DBSCAN fit dense/noise groups separately to one-dimensional changes in each machine/metric, with a dataset-specific neighborhood rule. In one machine, 15 jaw-position outliers included a 1.3 mm apparent shift near a documented calibration. Independently paired ion-chamber measurements supported selected output-change comparisons on only two machines/12 events, not all DBSCAN flags.
evidence.unknown: Temporal associations do not establish service causation or independently confirmed physical faults. Apparent jaw shifts after steering may be measurement artifacts. Acquisition timing and detector recalibration records were incomplete, and two machines lacked complete service histories. Clustering parameters were not optimized against prospective truth; noise-versus-cluster statistical comparisons are circular. No sensitivity/specificity, superiority to existing QA, safer treatment or patient benefit was established.
evidence.ai_role: DBSCAN learned density structure in longitudinal QA changes and flagged sparse observations, enabling targeted linkage of unusual measured signals to service documentation rather than a fixed list of expected calibration effects.
